content:
“And Agamemnon, lord of men, answered him in turn:

‘Son of Laertes, I rejoice to hear your word;
for you have set forth and recounted everything duly.
And these things I am willing to swear—indeed my spirit urges me—
and I will not swear falsely before heaven. But let Achilles
remain there for the present, though eager for battle;
and do the rest of you all remain gathered together, until the gifts
come out from the hut and we cut the solemn oaths.
And to you yourself I lay this charge and command:
choose the best young men of all the Achaeans
to bring from my ship the gifts which yesterday we promised
to give Achilles, and to lead here the women.
And let Talthybius quickly, throughout the wide camp of the Achaeans,
make ready a boar for me, to sacrifice to Zeus and to the Sun.’”

If you want, I can also give:
- a more literal line-by-line translation,
- a smoother poetic translation,
- or grammatical notes on difficult words.
